headline: Approved projects at 40 Eastview Street, 45 Katherine Drive, 127 Durant Street, and 211 Plain Street; continued 37-39 Roberts and 384 Butman Road.
summary: Four petitions were approved: a garage with bonus room at 40 Eastview Street, an addition at 45 Katherine Drive, a porch roof at 127 Durant Street, and a NAPA Auto Parts store at 211 Plain Street. Requests for 37-39 Roberts Street and 384 Butman Road were continued to the 10/15 meeting.
decisions: Approved ZBA-2026-33 for 40 Eastview Street with two conditions, 5-0.
Approved ZBA-2026-37 Variance for 127 Durant Street, 5-0.
Approved ZBA-2026-38 Special Permit for 211 Plain Street Unit 6A, 5-0.
Continued ZBA-2026-36 for 37-39 Roberts Street to the 10/15 meeting, 5-0.
Continued ZBA-2026-37 for 384 Butman Road to the 10/15 meeting, 5-0.

plain_text:
Lowell Zoning Board of Appeals Minutes 
9/14/2026 at 6:30 P.M.  
 
Note: These minutes are not completed verbatim. For further detail, contact the Division of 
Development Services, 375 Merrimack Street, Lowell, MA or refer to video recordings available online 
at www.LTC.org. 
 
Members Present: Chairman Pech, Vice Chair Callahan, Member McCarthy, Member Procope, Member 
Hovey, Member Shanahan 
 
Members Absent: Member Briere 
 
Others Present: Peter Cutrumbes, Assistant Planner 
 
The following represents the actions taken by the Zoning Board of Appeals at the 9/14/2026 meeting. This 
meeting was held in the  City Council Chamber . Attendees had the ability to participate via Zoom as 
permitted by Chapter 2 of the Acts of 2025, signed into law on March 28, 2025. 
 
Chairman Pech called the meeting to order at 6:30 PM. 
I. Continued Business 
 
II. New Business 
 
ZBA-2026-33  
Petition Type: Variance  
Applicant: Gene Espinola  
Property Located at: 40 Eastview Street, 01852  
Applicable Zoning Bylaws: Section 5.1  
Petition: The Lowell Zoning Board of Appeals will hold a public hearing to hear all interested 
persons relative to an application by Gene Espinola to construct a two -car garage with a bonus room 
above and connecting breezeway at 40 Eastview Street. The subject prope rty is located 
in the Suburban Single-Family zoning district. The proposal requires a Variance per Section 5.1 for relief 
from minimum front yard setback, the maximum Floor -Area-Ratio (FAR), and any other relief required 
under the City of Lowell Zoning Ordinance.   
 
On Behalf: 
Ken Lania, the applicant’s Engineer. Need relief because it is a corner lot. Need a front yard Variance. The 
proposal is 13.2 feet from the street. Need relief from FAR. The proposal will raise the FAR to 40% from 
31%. The maximum is 35%. This particular addition will help bring new life to a blighted structure. Existing 
driveway is where the new garage area is.
Speaking in Opposition:  
None 
 
Speaking in Favor: 
None 
 
Discussion: 
G. Procope said he does not have an issue with this. It is a natural fit in the neighborhood. No detriment 
to the area. D. McCarthy agreed that this application is not asking for a lot of relief. The front yard setbacks 
already exist. Relief mostly for the  dimensional on the garage and the FAR. Should use Engineering 
comments as conditions of approval. K. Lania said he is amenable. S. Callahan concurred with his fellow 
Board members. Asked what the dimensions of the bonus rooms are. K. Lania said he was not involved in 
the architectural plans but he did speak with the contractor and Mr. Espinola but confirmed that it is not 
going to be an ADU. S. Callahan asked for an estimate of the height. K. Lania said the second floor would 
be about 12x24. S. Callahan said it looks to be about 12 feet high. K. Lania said it is a 12 pitch. T. Hovey 
had no questions. D. Shanahan concurred. V. Pech said he has no concerns. 
 
Motion: 
D. McCarthy motioned to approve with conditions. T. Hovey seconded. The conditions were as follows: 
1. The applicant shall obtain a driveway paving permit to expand and/or repave the existing 
driveway.  
 
2. The applicant shall comply with all current 780CMR, 527 CMR 1.00, as well as any NPFA 
regulations that apply per occupancy type. 
The vote was unanimous (5-0). 
 
ZBA-2026-35  
Petition Type: Variance   
Applicant: Niranjan Bhagat  
Property Located at: 45 Katherine Drive, 01854  
Applicable Zoning Bylaws: Section 5.1   
Petition: The Lowell Zoning Board of Appeals will hold a public hearing to hear all interested 
persons relative to an application by Niranjan Bhagat to construct an addition at 45 Katherine Drive. The 
subject property is located in the Suburban Single -Family (SSF) zoning district. The project requires 
Variance approval per Section 5.1 for relief from the maximum Floor-Area-Ratio (FAR), and for any other 
relief required under the Lowell Zoning Ordinance.  
 
On Behalf: 
Niranjan Bhagat, the applicant. He summarized the addition to the rear of the house. FAR relief is needed. 
 
Speaking in Opposition:  
None 
 
Speaking in Favor: 
None
Discussion: 
D. McCarthy said this is a very minimal ask with the FAR going from .35 to .39. It looks like a great plan. 
Thankful for the diagram. P lenty of green space. S. Callahan said it is a minimal request for FAR. No 
concerns. T. Hovey said they are staying within the depth and width of the house. No issues. D. Shanahan 
said it is a minimal ask and he is in favor. G. Procope asked if the RFP sign was posted. N. Bhagat confirmed. 
V. Pech had no comments 
 
Motion: 
D. McCarthy motioned to approve. S. Callahan seconded. The vote was unanimous (5-0). 
 
ZBA-2026-37  
Petition Type: Variance  
Applicant: Luis Lora  
Property Located at: 127 Durant Street, 01850  
Applicable Zoning Bylaws: Section 5.1  
Petition: The Lowell Zoning Board of Appeals will hold a public hearing to hear all interested 
persons relative to an application by Luis Lora to construct a roof over his existing front porch at 127 
Durant Street. The subject property is located in  the Traditional Single-Family zoning district. The 
proposal requires a Variance per Section 5.1 for relief from the maximum Floor-Area-Ratio (FAR) and any 
other relief required under the City of Lowell Zoning Ordinance. 
 
On Behalf: 
Applicant’s representative (she did not provide name) . Just seeking roof over the porch. Gets icy and 
slippery during winter. Its already existing property —just an extension of the roof. Nothing about the 
architectural facade of the building is changing. 
 
Speaking in Opposition:  
None 
 
Speaking in Favor: 
None 
 
Discussion: 
S. Callahan said it is just a covering for the porch. Noted for his colleagues that the zoning rewrite may 
increase FAR requirements or eliminate them. No issue. T. Hovey had no questions. D. Shanahan said it is 
a completely minimal ask. Supportive. G. Procope in favor. D. McCarthy said he has no issues. Thank you 
for taking great care of the property. It is a safety problem and a minimal ask. V . Pech said it makes 
complete sense. 
 
Motion: 
D. McCarthy motioned to approve the Variance. G. Procope seconded. The vote was unanimous (5-0).
ZBA-2026-38  
Petition Type: Special Permit  
Applicant: RB Lowell Meadow Brook, LLC  
Property Located at: 211 Plain Street Unit 6A, 01852  
Applicable Zoning Bylaws: Section 5.1  
Petition: The Lowell Zoning Board of Appeals will hold a public hearing to hear all interested 
persons relative to an application by RB Lowell Meadow Brook, LLC to open a NAPA Auto Parts store at 
211 Plain Street Unit 6A. The subject property is located in the High Rise Commercial zoning district. The 
proposal requires a Special Permit per Section 12.4.b to operate  an auto parts store at this location and 
any other relief required under the City of Lowell Zoning Ordinance.  
 
On Behalf: 
George Theodorou. Applicant’s counsel. Special Permit to operate a retail facility over 5,000 square feet. 
Part of two open air shopping plazas in the Target plaza.  Will be adjacent to the new RMV site to be 
completed by this fall. Andrea Kiryacou, the applicant’s representative also on Zoom. DPD staff said it fits 
in with the use of the property. Over the years it has been difficult to lease this end of the plaza. There 
are over 150 parking spaces. RB Meadowbrook have been fantastic stewards of this property. 
 
Speaking in Opposition:  
None 
 
Speaking in Favor: 
None 
 
Discussion: 
T. Hovey had no questions. D. Shanahan said no questions. G. Procope had no questions, he is supportive. 
D. McCarthy said the owners of this plaza have done a great job keeping it vibrant. Glad to see a new use 
for the space. Deserving of the special permit. S . Callahan concurred with his colleagues. Owners have 
done a great job with the plaza. Immediately replace tenants when they leave.  V. Pech had no concerns. 
 
Motion: 
D. McCarthy motioned to approve the Special Permit. S. Callahan seconded. The vote was unanimous (5-
0). 
 
 
 
ZBA-2026-36  
Petition Type: Special Permit and Variance  
Applicant: Jeffrey Ciccone  
Property Located at: 37-39 Roberts Street, 01854  
Applicable Zoning Bylaws: Sections 4.3, 4.5, and 4.5  
Petition: The Lowell Zoning Board of Appeals will hold a public hearing to hear all interested 
persons relative to an application by Jeffrey Ciccone to retain the existing three-family home at 37 
Robert Street; and to construct a single-family home and Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) at 39 Robert 
Street. The subject property at 37 Robert Street is located in the Traditional Two-Family (TTF) zoning 
district. The subject property at 39 Robert Street is located in the Traditional Single-Family (TSF) zoning 
district. The proposal at 37 Robert Street requires a Variance per Section 5.1 for relief from minimum lot 
size, minimum lot area per dwelling unit (LA/DU), minimum side yard setbacks; a Variance per Section
4.3.5 (4) for relief from garage side yard setback; a Variance per Section 6.1.4 for relief from minimum 
off-street parking spaces; and any other relief required under the City of Lowell Zoning Ordinance. The 
proposal at 39 Robert Street requires a Variance per Section 5.1 for relief from minimum lot 
size, minimum lot area per dwelling unit (LA/DU), minimum frontage, maximum Floor-Area-Ratio 
(FAR), minimum lot width; and any other relief required under the City of Lowell Zoning Ordinance.  The 
proposals also require a modification of the Special Permit per Section 4.5 recorded on June 1, 1998, at 
the Middlesex North Registry of Deeds.  
 
On Behalf: 
Jonathan Stark-Sachs, the applicant’s representative.  Proposing to build a new dwelling. T here are t wo 
parcels currently shared but will be split . The Variances are consistent with the buildup of the 
neighborhood. Properties are in two different zoning districts. 37 Roberts is in Traditional Two Family and 
39 Roberts is in Traditional Single-Family. Showed the plans for both lots. The single-family dwelling would 
have an ADU. It sits within the setbacks and the height. In 1998 th e property got a Special Permit for the 
structure to be a three -family. The condition was that the vacant 39 Robert Street remain in common 
ownership with the existing 3 family home at 37 Robert. The lot was at some point overflow parking, but 
has not been used as that since at least 2020, when the applicant purchased it. It is just dirt and grass. 
Summarized the needed relief for the proposed single -family/ADU at 39 Robert Street. Splitting the lot 
also requires relief for the existing three -family structure at 37 Robert Street to remain in its condition. 
Summarized this relief. Both requests for belief are in the petition. This is just to allow the existing lot line 
of the two properties to be created for zoning purposes. Right now the lots are taxed as two separate lots. 
Parking variances needed because the condition from 1998 required 39 Roberts to be used as overflow 
parking. Asking for a “release” of that condition. The language to grant a variance standard statewide has 
changed from hardship to a “practical difficulty”. Enables the Board to have more flexibility.   The new 
legal language requires the Board to weigh the benefits to the appellant against the public interest, as 
well as the benefit of creating more housing.  Concluded by stating that much of the Variance relief 
required is due to the condition from 1998. The Variances are needed to operate the lots separately. The 
proposal helps increase the housing stock. Applicant canvassed the neighborhood and they have 
submitted a list of supporters. 
 
Speaking in Opposition:  
Curtis Lemay of 40 Robert Street. Abutter across the street. Member of the Pawtucketville  Citizens 
Council. Well versed with the property. Been at his property for almost 50 years. The lot in question used 
to be water but was filled in. A stipulation of the approval to make the building a three-family was to put 
in angled parking at 39 Robert Street. This was never done. The proposed structure will need at least six 
parking spaces and will only have room for two. Street parking is very congested in this area. Its too dense 
for the neighborhood. 
 
Speaking in Favor: 
None 
 
Discussion: 
Attorney stated that the two parking spaces provided for the proposed structure is conforming with 
zoning. ADU’s do not need parking if they are within half a mile of a bus stop, which they are. The minutes 
of the 1998 hearing did not require the lot to be paved. 
 
D. Shanahan stated 39 Roberts is zoned for single-family. The placement of a single-family dwelling would 
conform. New construction including an ADU is unusual, but not aware of anything that prohibits it. In
these circumstances though, it feels aggressive. Appreciates that some neighbors have signed in support. 
Noted the petition describes the project as constructing a single-family home with no mention of an ADU. 
G. Procope asked if Counsel saw the three conditions proposed by DPD. Counsel confirmed. G. Procope 
asked how many bedrooms are in the existing house. Counsel said 5. G. Procope said he would like to hear 
the opinion of his fellow Board members. D . McCarthy noted there are undersized lots in this 
neighborhood with single-family homes that don’t even have off-street parking and they could still build 
an ADU by right. Why did they not ask for the single-family and then ask for the ADU after? Understands 
the applicant is trying to be transparent but also it creates uncomfortable feelings around density. J. Stark-
Sachs said they did want to be fully transparent. Other towns have tried to create regulations that an 
existing single-family home had to be pre-existing for an ADU to be created. The AG has struck them down. 
D. McCarthy noted that there doesn’t seem to be evidence that the vacant lot was used as parking. How 
is it being used today? Are there any tenant agreements that allow them to park there? J. Stark-Sachs said 
the vacant lot is not used for parking. D. McCarthy said we do need the housing that this proposal provides, 
and he leans supportive. Understands that a lot of the Variances are from the existing structure. S. 
Callahan stated he has concerns about the project with the ADU. He believes t he proposed size of the 
ADU is in excess of the allowed size of an ADU. It can only be 50% of the area of the proposed structure, 
which is 600 square feet. The ADU is 900 square feet. Would like clarification. J. Starks-Sachs said that the 
state regulations define the gross floor area as including everything inside the footprint of the house. S. 
Callahan said he believed ADUs were for already existing structures. J. Stark-Sachs said they are amenable 
to a continuance if the Board wants more information on legal regulations around ADUs. T. Hovey said he 
appreciates the background. In 1998 the applicant stated they were going to combine both lots. They 
never were. Even if they were, they would still not be compliant with LA/DU. The “practical difficulties” in 
the new state law for Variance criteria  are self-imposed. The applicant knew there was a Special Permit 
when they bought it. Does not meet the intent of zoning. There are too many asks  for Variances on this. 
We do need housing, but not at the expense of the neighborhood. V. Pech said there may be a pathway, 
but he could not support this as i s. Could the client agree to a continuance to provide more information 
on ADU regulations and modify plans? Counsel was amenable.  
 
D. McCarthy asked the applicant to re -circulate a petition that shows there will be an ADU on the new 
single-family. The petition only says a single family. 
 
Motion: 
D. McCarthy motioned to continue the application to the 10/15 meeting. T. Hovey seconded. The vote 
was unanimous (5-0). 
 
ZBA-2026-37  
Petition Type: Variances  
Applicant: Mullane Construction, LLC  
Property Located at: 384 Butman Road, 01852  
Applicable Zoning Bylaws: Section 5.1  
Petition: The Lowell Zoning Board of Appeals will hold a public hearing to hear all interested 
persons relative to an application by Mullane Construction, LLC to construct a single -family home at 384 
Butman Road. The subject property is located in the Suburban Single -Family (SSF) zoning district. The 
project requires Variance approval per Section 5.1 for relief from  the minimum frontage, minimum lot 
area, and minimum lot area per dwelling unit requirements, and for any other relief required under the 
Lowell Zoning Ordinance.
On Behalf: 
Attorney John Geary. Summarized the project and the relief it needs. The nonconformities of the lot are 
common in the neighborhood. They demonstrated this in the GIS exhibit provided. The proposed home is 
modest in size. It contains 1440  square feet  of living space and two beds and two baths. This is not a 
cookie-cutter home. Built with the dimensions of the lot in mind. Meet the amount of required parking. 
The lot has 55 feet of frontage. This is comparable to the surrounding lots. This proposal is in accordance 
with the new Variance standards under MGL. The Board is required to weigh the benefits of the project 
against the detriments to the existing neighborhood, with a focus on constructing housing. Also r equires 
consideration of practical hardship. Client cannot do anything else with this lot. Regarding detriments to 
the neighborhood, the proposed home and lot fits the development pattern of the area. It would not be 
detrimental to the area. Not approving the Variances imposes a financial hardship on the property owner. 
This hardship was not self-created. The applicant purchased the lot with the understanding a home could 
be built. Prior to purchasing the lot, the applicant received a Building Permit to construct a home. Building 
Commissioner put stop work order at that time because he believed the permit may have been issued in 
error. They are amenable to the proposed conditions. They are in receipt of several letters of opposition 
from neighbors. J. Geary said they sent out the wrong mailing first with a different meeting date, but they 
re-sent the notices. They included a letter explaining the situation and it was still sent out prior to the two 
week deadline. The applicant also sent out letters to all of the list of abutters describing the project and 
providing his contact info to speak with any of the neighbors. The letters of opposition express concerns 
that Butman Road is narrow in this section and that additional on-street parking from this new home may 
make that more narrow. The applicant has designed a home that meets the required parking, the home 
is modest, and they have done what they can do to meet these concerns. Matt Hamor, the applicant’s 
engineer, summarized the site and floor plans. The home will connect to utilities on Butman. There is a 
10-foot easement on the lot that was supposed to be just for maintenance, but the verbiage was vague 
and may potentially be more encompassing. Pending approval, they would update the easement to be 
just for maintenance. The driveway will not encroach on the easement. The dwelling is 20x36. There is a 
shade tree at the front of the house. J. Geary said they believe they meet the  zoning requirements and 
they respectfully ask for approval. 
 
Speaking in Opposition:  
 
Brian Nowak, representing his mother Carol Nowak of 58 Wedgemere Drive . They have concerns about 
stormwater. The proposed stormwater system would work if the s oil types are as the applicant claimed, 
but they did not do soil testing. Water could flow onto 5 homes on Wedgemere. 
 
Melynda Grimmet at 388 Butman Road. Submitted a letter of opposition to the Board. The lot is 
undersized for the neighborhood. This is the applicant’s third attempt to build. She was the one who called 
Attorney Geary to inform him of the abutter’s notice discrepancy. They did not receive the new letter until 
the 2 nd. That is not two weeks prior. This  project is a self -inflicted hardship. Applicant bought the lot 
knowing the lot was undersized under zoning. The only hardship is they bought this undersized lot without 
checking first. A buyer creating a hardship for themselves is not covered by the law. Her husband Rob 
spoke. In 2016 the ZBA said they should construct something in collaboration with neighbors. They never 
did this. They left an open foundation. During their initial excavation in 2015, they knocked over the fence 
on the property within the maintenance easement. They never replaced it. They promised to pay to repair 
their fence, but they never did.  Neighbors have been responsible for the upkeep of the property.  
Application lists the wrong zoning district and the square footage/stories are not listed correctly. M. 
Grimmet spoke again. The house is built to the absolute maximum of every dimensional requirement. 
They would like to ask the Board if its  even a buildable lot. The lot used to be part of 376  Butman Road.
Massachusetts General Law said lots in common ownership are considered merged. Applicant should have 
to prove that it is legally separated. The applicant is not from Lowell. Butman is already a busy road and 
there are children outside playing. Butman has a serious on -street conges tion issue. Understands the 
parking is up to code. There will be runoff problems from the lot. The new fence location the  plans say 
will be replaced by the owner was not communicated. They destroyed their fence the first construction 
attempt. There is already an active construction site at 369 Butman Street. This did not need Variance 
approval. This has caused rodent issues, and a second site would cause more. The lots the applicant cites 
as also being undersized were all in place before the current zoning ordinance. The home is larger than 
most of the homes nearby. Asking for a denial If the Board is inclined to approve, they are asking for  the 
following: 
1. Require the applicant to correct and re-certify the application's internal inconsistencies described 
above before any vote is taken; 
2.  Require a chain-of-title analysis establishing the lot's buildable status under G.L. c. 40A, § 6; 
3. Require independent City Engineer or DPW review of the drainage and detention design;  
4. Require a pre -construction survey and a bonded guarantee protecting the easement and fence 
line at 388 Butman Road; and;  
5. Impose clear, enforceable conditions, with real consequences for noncompliance, given this 
applicant's documented history of beginning construction before this Board's own conditions 
were met. 
 
Bill Schmidt of 394 Butman Road. The dimensions of the lot do not come close to what is required. There 
is a significant erosion issue in the neighborhood currently. A construction company not being fully aware 
of the zoning requirements when purchasing is not a hardship. 
 
John Doyle of 352 Butman Road. Did not get mail notice but saw the sign. His nephew is in the construction 
business and he warned him the lot is too small. It is a bad idea to squeeze a two -story home next to a 
ranch. In 2016 the excavation near the fence made Ms. Grimmet’s fence cave in. 
 
Meaghan Sun of 376 Butman Road. Adjacent property. Her lot was previously attached in some manner 
to this lot. Contacted the prior owners to the owners she bought from, so two owners back. They had sold 
the lot as not a buildable lot and that it was meant to stay empty. She knew that the lot did not belong to 
her. Her child has grown up, learned to walk, next to a dangerous site. They took a long time to fill in the 
excavation. It was a safety risk to her kid and other kids in the  neighborhood. It took them going to the 
City to get the applicant to fill the hole. There are cars everywhere on the street. There is nowhere for 
children to walk or ride their bike. Neighborhoods becoming congested. 
 
Erik Gitschier, speaking in his private capacity as a citizen. Builders always cite housing production, but 
they also need to take into account the quality of the neighborhood. The lot is only 55% of the required 
lot size. The frontage is not enough. Butman road is squeezed down to nothing in this area. Not sure how 
it is even an accepted road at this point. 
 
Robin Costa of 387 Butman Road. Was at the meeting 10 years ago. Everything  on the plan is the same. 
The road is just as congested, if not more so.
Speaking in Favor: 
None 
 
 
 
Discussion: 
 
J. Geary said much has changed, including the MGL zoning criteria. They were updated this year. 
Requested relief is legitimate. They cannot build on this lot without the Variance. In terms of the notice—
he provided an affidavit for the record that the notice was done timely. The hardship is not self-inflicted. 
The permit was issued to the applicant before even purchasing  and then stopped by the Building 
Commissioner. Housing production is not just focused on affordable housing. M. Hamor said they would 
be doing boring and soil testing before any stormwater detention system was even installed. They work 
with the City’s stormwater team on these things. 
  
D. McCarthy asked why the foundation is in already. J. Geary said it is footings. Result of the first permit 
being issued in 2016. Applicant obtained permit , closed on the property, cleared the lot, installed the 
footings, and then the Building Commissioner issued a stop -work because he thought the permit  was 
issued in error. Eventually the footings were covered up and the lot remains as it is. D. McCarthy asked if 
there was a hole for the partial basement. J. Geary said that a hole was dug but the footings were 
eventually filled in and covered over. D. McCarthy said there is a lot of animosity between the neighbors 
and the builder. It is a significantly undersized lot. It does seem to merit a discussion because so many lots 
in the neighborhood are undersized. Ones that are not even that old. His brother owned a lot that was a 
similar size further up the street. Asked M. Hamor about drainage. They are creating a terrace effect. 
There are two relatively shallow slopes with levels in between. How does that affect drainage? Does it 
affect drainage across the street? M. Hamor said there is a catch basin on Butman Road for the drainage 
coming across the street. The ir proposed  system is required to detain 1 inch of rainfall for the total 
impervious area on the lot. It will be a subsurface infiltration system. Water will be taken into subsurface 
chambers and reintroduced into the underlying soils that then interact with the groundwater. D. McCarthy 
said that they are also producing infiltration via the terracing of the site. M. Hamor said that is correct. 
The Stormwater Permit is meant to address all of these issues. There will be a deep hole soil test prior to 
installation. There is an even more detailed plan done to get the stormwater permit. D . McCarthy asked 
if a single -family would have a significant effect on traffic. M. Hamor said in his experience the 
construction of a single -family home does not create additional issues. An entire traffic analysis would 
show this. D. McCarthy said ADUs are by-right in the neighborhood. Told the neighbors they could all have 
them, without even coming before the Board, making the traffic issue worse. The project meets a lot of 
criteria for FAR, green space, setbacks, etc. Wants to hear other members thoughts.  
 
S. Callahan said he appreciates residents voicing their opinions. Thanked Attorney Geary for re-sending 
notice. One of the abutters noted that on the application they listed UMF as the zoning district. They 
would condition an approval on amending that. Understands the concerns. However, the Commonwealth 
has changed zoning variance criteria. They cann ot use their old standards. There is a practical difficulty 
for the petitioner on this. He purchased the lot with the understanding it could be built on. They have to 
weigh this practical difficulty against the public good. He u nderstands the neighbors concerns about 
traffic, stormwater, etc. On the other side  of the argument , they have a new unit that would increase 
housing stock and increase the tax base for the City. It meets the intent of zoning. As lot size is concerned, 
it is  true that  almost all the lots in the area that are also undersized. Noted all these lots in the
neighborhood were all created in  1966, at the same time. He appreciates the neighbors coming out but 
he has to follow what is laid out by the law.  
 
T. Hovey noted the deed is not included with the packet. He believes there is self -imposed hardship. The 
applicant knew the required lot size when purchasing. Understands owner believed he could build. Have 
to hit three conditions. He does not believe the project meets the intent of zoning. Z oning requirements 
in the City have changed since the lot was created. They made the neighborhood SSF for a reason. The 
City’s goal with their most recent zoning was to require larger lot sizes in that district. If one of the 
conditions are not meant, the project cannot be approved.  
 
D. Shanahan said the Variance for the frontage is consistent with the neighborhood. The project would 
not stick out in the neighborhood. It is a modest house. Its narrow. Has an issue with an almost 50% 
reduction in the lot requirement. 
 
G. Procope said this is a tough project. He was concerned driving around the area about the slope and the 
stormwater assessment. Plan does show how abutters on Wedgemere would be protected. All in all he 
agrees that under the changes in MGL their hands are tied. Concerned  about the relationship between 
the developer and the abutters. He believes in the voices of neighborhoods. Suggested maybe applicant 
could work with neighbors. 
 
V. Pech said he appreciates everyone coming to the meeting. It provides valuable insight. The relief on 
paper is for lot area and frontage relief. Understands the concerns of the neighbors. He believes the 
Variance meets some of the criteria but not all of them. All of them need to be satisfied, so he can’t vote
